SourcesBox score, game stories and the drawn play

Box score from the Cavaliers' 115–107 win over the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Nov 11, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the Associated Press (via CBS Sports and theScore), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker) and the New York Post (via Yahoo Sports). All 115 Cleveland points and all 107 New York points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (59–53 at the half, matching the AP). Cleveland's 12-point lead (33–21 late in the first quarter, which Field Level Media also reports) and New York's 2-point lead are read from the CBS play-by-play. Team totals (free throws 20 of 25 to 11 of 11, rebounds 50–42, blocks 9–4, steals 8–5, assists 23–33) are CBS's. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games: Cleveland 6–6 and sixth in the East, Miami 5–6.

The Cavaliers led 95–85 with 8:25 left before New York went on a 14–4 run to tie it at 99 (AP; the CBS play-by-play has Josh Hart's layup tying it with 5:36 left). Harden came in averaging 15.3 points on 36.4 percent shooting (AP via theScore); 32 is his season high. Brunson took no free throws and New York took 11 to Cleveland's 25 (CBS box score). The win ended Cleveland's two-game losing streak (losses to New York on Nov 7 and at Charlotte on Nov 9, from the site's results) and a five-game losing run against the Knicks dating to last May's Eastern Conference finals (Field Level Media, New York Post). Cleveland plays at Miami on Friday at 8:00 PM ET, an NBA Cup group game (AP preview via Yahoo Sports).

The play of the game is an original illustration of James Harden's unassisted pull-up 3-pointer with 4:22 left, which broke a 101–101 tie and put Cleveland ahead for good (CBS play-by-play; Field Level Media and the New York Post have the same clock, the AP has 4:21). It came after Mitchell rebounded a Karl-Anthony Towns miss, and New York called timeout right after. The play-by-play calls it a pull-up; the recaps don't describe the move further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Harden's listed 6-foot-5 and 220 pounds (RealGM), with arms scaled to the 6-foot-11 wingspan in his 2009 pre-draft measurements (SLAM), in Cleveland's road wine with No. 1. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with our default skin tone. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
